links.outcome: Calibration of PsyMetRiC before vs after local logistic recalibration
links.effect: Calibration intercept improved from 0.16 to 0.01 (full) and -0.14 to 0.01 (partial); discrimination unchanged (C 0.72/0.70); net benefit improved further after recalibration.
links.quote: Following recalibration of PsyMetRiC-Fi to account for population differences, calibration of both models improved substantially with no detriment to discriminative accuracy.

links.outcome: Miscalibration of UK-developed model in Finnish sample with differing population characteristics
links.effect: Finnish sample differed from UK development sample on most sociodemographic, lifestyle and biochemical characteristics; PsyMetRiC full model underpredicted and partial model overpredicted risk.
links.quote: The Finnish sample differed from the UK PsyMetRiC development sample on most sociodemographic, lifestyle and biochemical characteristics (Table 1 ).

links.outcome: Discrimination and net benefit of PsyMetRiC compared with FINDRISC on same data
links.effect: C-statistic 0.72 (full) and 0.70 (partial) vs 0.63 for FINDRISC; at 15% threshold net benefit 0.13 for PsyMetRiC-Fi vs 0.01 for FINDRISC.
links.quote: Both PsyMetRiC versions showed superior discriminative accuracy in this early psychosis population compared with using FINDRISC.

links.outcome: Local historical data validation of predictive model against reference standard
links.effect: External validation in 278 Finnish patients found acceptable discrimination but miscalibration that required recalibration, showing local validation identified performance problems.
links.quote: Calibration plots (Figure 2 , Figure S3 ) show varying degrees of miscalibration for PsyMetRiC across imputed datasets, with predominantly risk underprediction in the full-model, and overprediction in the partial-model.

links.effect: PsyMetRiC full model predominantly underpredicted risk; partial model overpredicted risk across imputed datasets.
